expectedToChange.reason: Wave B-1 batch B1, LCP delivery. The homepage hero gains a hero-scoped sizes="100vw" in place of the build transform's default (which tops out at 800px and describes a contained card), and the preload gains an imagesrcset/imagesizes generated from the same candidate list the element carries. The browser therefore selects a correctly-sized candidate for the LCP photograph -- MEASURED in a real browser against the built site: w_1920 at 1440 and w_400 at 390, exactly one hero request per width, where it previously fetched w_1200 for the preload and w_800 for the element. WHAT THE HARNESS ACTUALLY MEASURED (not predicted): changedPct 0.000% at 1440 and 0.001% at 390 -- the re-resampled photograph is below the metric's per-pixel tolerance, so this waiver consumes almost nothing and is kept as the declaration of intent rather than as cover. Height delta 0 at both widths. WHY THIS SHAPE AND NOT A pageOverride: route '/' may never carry a pageOverride. The F1/F1b calibration fixtures evaluate '/' against the shipped config, so a home-page override disarms the harness's own self-test -- a property that has caught bad '/' entries three times (see _notes.residualsNotDeclared). A changedPct waiver is the compliant shape precisely BECAUSE the shift gates are unwaivable and stay live. THEY STAY LIVE AND THEY ARE RED: layoutShiftMaxPx 51 at 1440 and shiftCoverage 0.926 at 390. That is recorded here as a red, NOT waived and NOT overridden -- per _notes.authority, a budget and a fixture that disagree are renegotiated in the plan, never tuned here to make a run pass. The evidence that it is not layout movement, measured pixel-by-pixel on the two captures: the rows that differ are 0-899 at 1440 and 0-719 at 390, i.e. exactly the 100vh hero band, and EVERY row below the hero is byte-identical, with total page height unchanged (7036 and 10635) and max per-channel delta 33/38. Nothing on the page moved; the row-signature matcher has no tolerance for a re-resampled photograph and mismatches rows inside the hero band. Escalated to the relay rather than absorbed. Retirement: tracked in the ROADMAP, executed by B6, which must PRESERVE this entry until the baseline advances past it (the schema has no expiry field for expectedToChange). DEPLOY-1 FIX ROUND ADDENDUM (2026-08-02), two further reasons `/` moves, both deliberate and neither one waiving anything new. (1) THE HERO SCRIM: --hero-scrim was declared at styles.css:169 and painted by nothing -- .hero-content's comment claimed contrast was 'carried by the scrim' while the only thing carrying it was filter: brightness(0.7). Jen's Stage 3 ruling puts it on .hero::after. Measured against the brightest pixel behind each element at 1440, h1 goes 1.77:1 -> 5.86:1 and the subtitle 1.79:1 -> 5.89:1. This is PAINT ONLY -- an inset:0 pseudo-element with pointer-events:none, no box in flow -- so it moves changedPct at both widths and moves NOTHING in layout. The shift gates stay live against it and must. (2) THE HERO CLEARANCE FIX, which is layout and is confined to <=768px: the hero now reserves the fixed nav's band (--nav-band) and centres in what is left, because it had been centring into a strip whose top 91px the nav paints over, putting the h1 behind the nav at 360-430. At 1440 the rule does not apply and geometry is byte-for-byte unchanged -- the 1440 capture moves for the scrim alone. At 390 the hero band moves down 45.5px; page height is UNCHANGED at 390 (the box stays 80vh and the content re-centres) and grows only at 360, which is not a captured width. NOTE PRECISELY what this does to the shift reds recorded above: they were already red and already REFUSED, and the rows they implicate are the hero band (0-719 at 390), which is exactly the band this fix moves. They stay red, they stay refused, and they are NOT re-litigated, re-waived or overridden here -- `/` still carries no pageOverride, by the rule stated above. What changes is that part of the 390 residual now has an intended layout cause on top of the resampling one. Retirement remains B6's, at baseline advance. MEASURED AFTERWARDS, 5748de8..b1576e1, replacing the prediction above with the run's own numbers. Of 38 page/width comparisons exactly TWO carry any changed pixels and both are `/`; the other 36 are 0.000%, so the wave's pixel-control property is intact and neither fix leaked off this route. `/`@1440: changedPct 7.519% (waived), layoutShiftMaxPx 0, heightDelta 0, shiftCoverage 0.888. `/`@390: changedPct 4.188% (waived), layoutShiftMaxPx 60, heightDelta 0, shiftCoverage 0.984. Read the 1440 row carefully -- shift 0 and height 0 are the direct confirmation that the scrim is paint only, since 1440 is the width where the clearance rule does not apply. THE TWO REDS SWAPPED METRIC AND WIDTH and that is worth stating so nobody reads it as a gate newly broken or newly excused. Before this round they were layoutShiftMaxPx 51 at 1440 and shiftCoverage 0.926 at 390. Now they are shiftCoverage 0.888 at 1440 and layoutShiftMaxPx 60 at 390. The 1440 red is the same instrument limitation as before wearing a different name: nothing moved there, but the row-signature matcher has no per-pixel tolerance and cannot re-find rows whose luminance the scrim changed, which is the row-matcher tolerance issue already queued post-wave. The 390 red is REAL LAYOUT and intended -- the hero content moves down 45.5px to clear the nav -- and 390's coverage incidentally recovered from 0.926 to 0.984. Both remain REFUSED RESIDUALS: nothing here is waived, overridden or re-litigated, `/` still carries no pageOverride, and retirement is still B6's at baseline advance. _notes.authority: These are the ONLY budgets. lib/gate.mjs reads them and defaults nothing; no threshold is written down anywhere else in the harness. If a budget and a fixture in visual-diff.test.mjs disagree, the fixture wins and the budget is renegotiated in the plan, never tuned here to make a run pass.
_notes.widths: Capture widths in CSS pixels. 1440 = desktop, 390 = iPhone-class mobile. An empty list is a hard error: a run that captures nothing cannot pass.
_notes.maxLayoutShiftPx: Budget from the redesign acceptance criterion. Gated against layoutShiftMaxPx -- the MAXIMUM observed row displacement, not the p99. A 6px sitewide button move touches few enough rows that a percentile hides it, and hiding it is exactly the defect this harness was repaired for.
_notes.minShiftCoverage: Fraction of structured baseline rows that must be found again in the candidate. This is what catches the two failures the pixel and p99 metrics are blind to: content that moved further than diff.mjs's 240px search window, and a page whose content changed outright. Both report a shift of zero; both drop coverage to near zero.
_notes.maxChangedPct: Percentage of the page that may look different before it is treated as a regression. Cosmetic anti-aliasing noise sits well under 0.5%.
_notes.maxScaleDivergence: How far the two capture widths of ONE page may disagree about that page's affine SCALE. Under the affine model this is the sharper of the two divergence checks: both widths render from the same stylesheet, so a leading change should compress them by a comparable ratio even though their layouts differ. 0.05 is a first calibration and should be revisited once real per-page scales from a leading change have been seen; tighten it, do not loosen it, without saying why.
_notes.minFitConfidence: Fraction of a page's ELIGIBLE rows (those whose row signature is distinctive enough to take part in the fit at all -- rows of repeating texture are excluded from both sides of the ratio) that the affine fit must explain before the fit counts as a fit at all. Below this the run FAILS with an explicit model-does-not-fit reason rather than reporting residuals against a fit that does not hold -- if the model is wrong, every shift number beside it is measured against nothing. Deliberately NOT waivable (see UNWAIVABLE in lib/gate.mjs) and NOT overridable per page: a page the instrument cannot describe is a human conversation, not a config line. 0.75 separates the observed cases by a wide margin -- a real leading change fits at 0.958, a constant-offset model on the same page fitted at 0.034 -- but it is a first calibration, not a measured threshold.
_notes.maxOffsetDivergencePx: How far the two capture widths of ONE page may disagree about that page's estimated global vertical offset. Deliberately generous: the 1440px and 390px layouts are different documents and a leading change legitimately compresses them by different amounts, so this is a 'wildly differently' detector rather than a precision gate. The sharp signal alongside it needs no budget at all -- if one width GREW while the other SHRANK, that is reported regardless of magnitude, because no single spacing change does that. 400 is a first calibration and should be revisited once real per-page offsets from a leading change have been seen; tighten it, do not loosen it, without saying why.
_notes.expectedToChange: Per-metric waivers, not a blanket pass. Shape: { "route": "/about/", "reason": "new hero type scale", "waive": ["changedPct"] }. Waivable: changedPct, heightDelta, structural. NEVER waivable: layoutShiftMaxPx, shiftCoverage -- a config that tries is a hard error. A page may waive changedPct and remain shift-gated; that is the whole point of the restructure. Bare route strings are rejected so an old-shape config cannot silently keep its old blanket-waiver meaning.
_notes.pageOverrides: Moves ONE named budget on ONE named page, in the direction that metric's TYPE allows, for a stated reason, until a stated date. Shape: { "page": "/about/", "metric": "maxLayoutShiftPx", "value": 24, "reason": "new hero type scale moves the fold ~20px, approved in the Wave A design review", "expires": "2026-09-30" }. CEILINGS (maxLayoutShiftPx, maxChangedPct) may only be RAISED, capped at 100x the global -- loud is fine, infinite is not, so value: 999999 is rejected. The FLOOR (minShiftCoverage) may only be LOWERED, bounded to [0.75, 1) -- lowering is the shippable direction for a deliberate restyle, and below 0.75 a quarter of the page's rows could not be matched at all, which is a human conversation rather than a config line. An override can NEVER disable a metric and can never rescue a page whose shift could not be measured. Rejected on load: unknown metric, wrong direction, out of bounds, missing or empty reason, missing or malformed expiry, an expiry more than 90 days out, a duplicate page/metric pair. An EXPIRED override fails the run loudly rather than lapsing back to the global budget, so a temporary allowance cannot quietly become permanent. Overrides affect only the page and metric they name. This exists so a deliberate restyle is shippable under review; the global budgets above stay unwaivable and are not to be lowered to make a run pass.
_notes.expectedRedirects: Client-side redirects the capture is expected to observe, as route -> settled destination. A redirect that is not declared, points somewhere else, or stops happening fails the run. Without this the harness screenshots the destination page under the source route's name and reports it as unchanged. /gallery/ and /process/ genuinely redirect today (verified 2026-07-30).
_notes.wp1b: WP-1b's recorded coverage figures were measured while the reveal pin was INERT (it still named the six pre-1b class names) and carry unquantifiable observer-race noise on reveal-heavy pages. They are not reproducible under the repaired harness (077ce33) and must not be quoted as a baseline. The batch's conclusions stand on its other evidence (DOM certificate, computed-rhythm suite, isolation probes).
_notes.stalePin: BLOCKER found 2026-07-31 during the Jen Stage 3 certification, and it invalidates this harness's reveal handling for every run since WP-1b. The capture pin at scripts/lib/capture.mjs (the rule that forces every scroll-reveal target to its settled visible state, so below-fold content is captured deterministically) still names the SIX PRE-WP-1b classes: .fade-in, .slide-up, .slide-left, .slide-right, .scale-in, .gallery-item--reveal. WP-1b collapsed all six into .reveal. Measured against the current build: those six selectors match ZERO elements, and the 206 elements carrying .reveal are matched by NOTHING in the pin. The pin has been inert since WP-1b landed. Consequence, stated plainly: below-fold reveal content is captured in whatever state the IntersectionObserver happened to have reached, which is timing-dependent -- exactly the non-determinism the pin exists to remove. Stage 3's F5 changes WHEN the hidden state is applied (parse time instead of DOMContentLoaded), so it shifts that timing and the run reports large diffs on content pages: / 7.6%/20.0%, /saunas/ and /gallery/ 12.3%/39.1%, /faq/ coverage 0.63, /contact/ shift 239px. Pages with no reveal-heavy below-fold content came back clean and are the control: /about/ 0.00%, /process/ 0.00%, /warranty/ 0.00%, /privacy/ 0.00%, /booking-ops.html 0.00% coverage 1.000 -- all PASS. A batch whose CSS-only items are provably DOM-neutral cannot legitimately move /saunas/ by 39% while leaving /about/ at zero. NO expectedToChange entries and NO pageOverrides were written from these numbers. Declaring a measurement taken through a broken instrument as expected is how noise becomes a permanent waiver. The pin is repaired FIRST, as its own reviewed commit by the harness's implementer, and only then is this batch re-measured -- the same rule the plan sets for every other instrument change. Until then the Stage 3 visual certification is OPEN, not passed and not waived. It also reframes the WP-1b record above: that run's coverage collapse was attributed entirely to the rhythm change, and some of it may be this.
_notes.residualsNotDeclared: Three classes from the polish-batch re-measure are deliberately NOT declared, because the mechanism refuses them by design: /faq/@390 coverage 0.627 (below the 0.75 absolute floor - C35 rewrites every question node; a human conversation, had: Jen's rendered review passed it), and fit-confidence failures on /@390 (0.706) and /saunas/ /gallery/@390 (0.565) - fitConfidence is unwaivable and non-overridable. These stay red as truth-tellers until the next baseline advance retires the comparison. ADDITIONALLY: / (home) carries NO shift override even though its 30px@1440 is fully attributed — the F1/F1b calibration fixtures evaluate route '/' against the shipped config, so any home-page shift override disarms the harness's own self-test (this property has now caught bad overrides three times: WP-1a's 18, and the reviewer's+orchestrator's own entry on 2026-07-31). The calibration route stays un-overridden by RULE; home's attributed residual is a truth-teller until the baseline advances.
_notes.b4ShiftOverrides: Wave B-1 B4 deliberately adds NO maxLayoutShiftPx override, although plan §B4 item 6 anticipated one. Measured 2026-08-02: max shift on /saunas/ is 2px at 1440 and 1px at 390, inside the 4px global budget, so an override would be an unconsumed waiver -- which this config's own B6 pruning item calls a live hazard. The plan expected a shift because the page loses ~40% of its height; it does not follow, because what was deleted sat BELOW most of the page's stable content and the affine model absorbs the displacement as offset rather than as per-row shift. The two 40px /saunas/+/gallery/ overrides still in pageOverrides are Wave A's and are now unconsumed too; B6 prunes them with the rest.
